title: Resting potential of distant cells controls oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Resting potential of distant cells controls oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The resting membrane potentials of cells located at a distance from oncogene-expressing cells are critical for whether those oncogene-expressing cells go on to form tumors in vivo, as shown in Xenopus laevis tadpoles injected with human oncogenes.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Extending prior work focused on the bioelectric state of cancer cells themselves, we show for the first time that the resting potentials of distant cells are critical for oncogene-dependent tumorigenesis.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “Abstract”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos/tadpoles injected with human or Xenopus oncogene mRNAs (Xrel3, Gli1, KRASG12D)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The intervention and outcome are direct and the publication reports several contrasts. Public article-level measurements allow checking the restricted Xenopus result, but incomplete raw data and mechanistic confounding prevent full resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare tumor-like-structure incidence in embryos with the same oncogene expression but remote hyperpolarizing versus matched control manipulations, verifying spatial separation and Vmem change. A reproducible incidence difference supports remote voltage causality.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Remote channel expression may have effects not mediated solely by voltage.

Individual embryo data are not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.95
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Remote hyperpolarization versus tumor incidence is a concrete contrast, and the paper publishes the summary rates for more than one oncogene. Those summaries can be checked for direction and reported significance. They cannot be recomputed from raw embryos, and they cover one amphibian assay rather than tumorigenesis in general, so the broad claim is only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score tumor-like-structure incidence when oncogene mRNA and a hyperpolarizing reagent are placed in separate blastomeres, with voltage confirmed at the remote site. A lower incidence only when the remote site is hyperpolarized would support a long-range voltage requirement; no change, or a requirement for local voltage only, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Blastomere separation is a fate-map proxy for distance, and mRNA injections carry nonspecific effects.

Embryo-level voltage and tumor scores are not in a public file.
